claim_ceiling: Visual design input only; no source, runtime, rendered-app, accessibility, device, privacy/legal, distribution, or release claim.

cross_cutting.contract: Every compact, regular, and accessibility-size layout preserves object identity, full consequence copy, and all actions without horizontal scrolling or semantic truncation.
cross_cutting.title: Dynamic Type resilience

cross_cutting.contract: Keyboard, Switch Control, and focus movement follow native order; dismissal, mutation, recovery, and resumed interruption restore focus to the originating object or next truthful state.
cross_cutting.title: Keyboard and focus continuity

cross_cutting.contract: System, light, and dark appearances use semantic tokens and preserve hierarchy, privacy, contrast, and state meaning; appearance never changes product behavior.
cross_cutting.title: Light and dark behavior

cross_cutting.contract: Copy expands, wraps, pluralizes, and mirrors for locale without hiding object meaning, time semantics, consequences, controls, or trust context.
cross_cutting.title: Localization and long-copy stress

cross_cutting.contract: Motion communicates continuity, route depth, accepted mutation, reflow, closure, and recovery; restrained haptics confirm meaningful selection, snap, success, conflict, or destructive confirmation and never carry meaning alone.
cross_cutting.title: Motion and haptic specification

cross_cutting.contract: Shape, label, value, hierarchy, and accessible state carry every status; color, material, motion, and spatial position remain supporting cues only.
cross_cutting.title: Non-color semantics

cross_cutting.contract: Object transforms, rail movement, reflow previews, disclosure, and completion use immediate state changes or restrained fades while preserving announcements, causal order, and focus.
cross_cutting.title: Reduce Motion

cross_cutting.contract: Materials become opaque semantic surfaces with equivalent grouping, depth, selection, warning, and contrast; no state relies on blur or translucency.
cross_cutting.title: Reduce Transparency

cross_cutting.contract: Design anatomy assumes native NavigationStack, sheets, full-screen covers, controls, lists, grids, scroll views, focus APIs, accessibility actions, and semantic design-system components; custom rendering requires a semantic native equivalent.
cross_cutting.title: Native SwiftUI plausibility

cross_cutting.contract: Reading order begins with destination and primary object, then current state and consequence, followed by actions and contextual Trust; custom actions mirror every gesture and focus returns predictably.
cross_cutting.title: VoiceOver reading order

journeys.accessibility: Consequences, scope, progress, and restored state are announced; destructive choices have explicit labels and focus returns to the surviving object or safe owner.
branches: Restore into an existing local graph
Reset local data after separately confirmed consequence review

journeys.commit_boundary: The separately confirmed restore, Trash, reset, or permanent-delete command is the only mutation boundary.
journeys.failure: Validation, storage, or import failure leaves canonical local data intact and quarantines suspect input.
journeys.interruption_resume: Resume from the last validated non-mutating step and revalidate package, free space, authorization, and current graph.
journeys.offline: Backup, restore, Trash, and local reset remain locally operable; optional continuity is not required.
preconditions: Local store is readable or repairably degraded
A rollback or export path is identified where feasible

journeys.rollback: Restore reverses Trash; accepted reset or permanent deletion follows its predeclared irreversible boundary and rollback reference.
tests: VoiceOver and Dynamic Type consequence review

happy_path: Review only material metadata and fit

journeys.offline: Classification, draft durability, local save, placement, Receipt, and replay work without account or network.
preconditions: Current surface context is known but non-authoritative
Canonical object owners can validate commands
journeys.recovery: Retry a failed attachment or placement, remove only the failed attachment, edit the proposal, or keep a safe unresolved draft.
journeys.rollback: Undo a safe recent save or use the created object's owning edit or Trash flow; original Capture evidence remains receipted.
journeys.title: Capture intent to canonical placement

nonvisual_sources.rationale: Concurrency, deterministic runtime, error-boundary, dependency, and platform mechanics constrain implementation and proof but do not independently define a frame; their visible consequences remain governed by mapped product, state, accessibility, and SwiftUI requirements.

Measured latency, memory, energy, and scale budgets constrain implementation acceptance rather than frame anatomy; loading, degradation, interruption, and recovery presentations are mapped separately.

Fixture, test-layer, mutation, migration, privacy, accessibility, and performance evidence rules define proof construction rather than visual composition; the user-visible contracts under test are mapped separately.

Validation, release, issue-readiness, review, governance, authorization, and claim-ceiling requirements govern acceptance and handoff rather than visual composition; all visible product obligations remain mapped through their owning requirements.
